auditor_value: Only when the projectile is launched from and lands on the same horizontal level (ground-to-ground), with g constant and no air resistance.

findings.quote: The formulas R = u²sin2θ/g, T = 2u sinθ/g and H = u²sin²θ/(2g) are derived by setting the net vertical displacement to zero when the particle lands.
findings.note: True for R and T, false for H: the maximum-height formula comes from setting the vertical velocity to zero at the highest point (v_y² = u_y² − 2gH), not from the landing condition. The stated derivation is wrong for one of the three formulas named.
findings.fix: The formulas R = u²sin2θ/g and T = 2u sinθ/g are derived by setting the net vertical displacement to zero when the particle lands; H = u²sin²θ/(2g) is derived by setting the vertical velocity to zero at the highest point.

findings.quote: State the condition in full; this is the final answer.

findings.fix: So the three formulas can be used directly only when the particle is projected from and lands on the same horizontal level, with g constant and no air resistance.

notes: The final answer (same-level projection, constant g, no air resistance) is the standard and correct condition; the defects are in the explanation, not the answer.
